findings.reason: without scoping §10 to plans the service is not queueing, a node builds an obligation that fires never and a gate that can only be made green by disabling §7 in the test.
findings.text: §10 raises an obligation for "each of its plans in which §4's read says at least one implementable section may be queued and has no request", while §7 (line 75) has the admit service file a request for "every implementable section that §4's read says may be queued and that has none", so after both land the set §10 watches is emptied by every admit pass and the obligation can never be carried — the section does not say it covers only the plans the service does not queue (the per-project switch off, or a coordinator's queue hold).

findings.reason: one added assertion closes the only half of the deliverable the gate leaves unproven, and the plan's own earlier findings were acted on for this same shape.
findings.text: §10's deliverable requires the obligation to name "the plan, the count of such sections and the whole-plan command", but its gate asserts only the count ("carries one obligation naming three") and that the named command clears it, so an obligation that omits the plan name passes, which breaks the case of a coordinator owning several plans at once.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited commits `b3d730c8e1`, `b5444d24ba` and `74fd70f0e7` all resolve as commits in this repository, `building-a-plan-queues-all-of-it` exists with an `s3` section, and `resolve_plan_coordinators` and the obligation-kind surface §10 relies on both exist.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §10's gate proves the obligation's count and command but never asserts that the obligation names its plan, which the deliverable also requires and which is the only way a coordinator owning several plans can tell the obligations apart.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — each arm's log sits under the run directory with its revision, literal command and a closing `EXIT=` line, which is durable and openable after the run.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s10's title, prose and `tests/test_an_owner_is_told_of_unqueued_work.py` carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and state the mechanism rather than the tracker entry.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §10's endpoint is unreachable whenever §7 is on: §7 files a request for exactly "every implementable section that §4's read says may be queued and that has none", which is precisely the predicate §10 raises its obligation for, so the obligation would never fire, and §10's stated rationale ("nothing tells a coordinator when that stops being true") is contradicted by §7 resolving that state without telling anyone.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §10 delivers one obligation kind on one surface, and the `_document` change only re-declares the split of 7.5 to 11.5 effort and the new s7–s10 sections, each with a single deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` now wires s4 to `building-a-plan-queues-all-of-it#s3` (which exists and is implementable), s7 to s3+s4, s8 to s7, and s9/s10 to s4, and each of those matches what the section's text consumes; no needed edge is missing and none points at the wrong node.
